citeAs: Cheng, G., Han, J., and Lu, X. (2016). Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art. Proceedings of the IEEE.
creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu (Northwestern Polytechnical University)
description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a freely and publicly available benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification. It contains 31,500 RGB remote sensing images divided into 45 scene classes, with 700 images per class, and was designed to provide large scale, rich image variations, and high within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
name: NWPU-RESISC45
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Images were extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth and organized into 45 scene classes. The dataset construction process involved manually selecting representative scene categories and manually curating image samples for each class.
rai:dataBiases: The paper states that the dataset includes images from more than 100 countries and regions, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies, reflecting an explicit design choice to improve diversity. It also states that images were carefully selected under different weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales to increase variation and reduce dataset simplicity.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by first selecting 45 representative scene classes. The authors investigated classes from existing datasets to form 30 widely used categories, then searched Web of Science and Google Scholar with keywords such as "OBIA", "GEOBIA", "land cover classification", "land use classification", "geographic image retrieval", and "geospatial object detection" to select 15 additional classes. Images were then extracted by experts in remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth, covering more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data were remote sensing images from Google Earth, which superimposes satellite imagery, aerial photography, and GIS on a 3D globe.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was created and released in 2016.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The paper emphasizes that the dataset is challenging because of high within-class diversity and between-class similarity, with semantically overlapping fine-grained classes such as circular versus rectangular farmland and commercial versus industrial area. It also notes that most scene classification methods still rely only on overhead imagery, implying limits for some semantic distinctions without complementary data sources.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted from Google Earth and standardized to 256×256 pixels in RGB color space. The dataset includes scene classes with spatial resolutions varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most classes, except island, lake, mountain, and snowberg, which have lower spatial resolutions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as supporting intelligent earth observation applications such as natural hazards detection, land use and land cover determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for remote sensing image scene classification and to enable the community to develop, evaluate, and compare data-driven algorithms, especially deep learning-based methods.
